answer: In my distributed systems lab, we bind each agent’s rate limits to a terrace validation scheme, where identities must wander through a dune of past work to prove genuineness. Each fake identity must resolve a unique cryptographic trail, burning 0.25s per head—the system serialized by linear history checks, no parallelization allowed. The cost compounds nonlinearly, forcing attackers to pay in unbatchable time per Sybil.
